paragraphs.en: Research sometimes proves, with {data} , what we more or less already know ( {e.g.} Exercise is good for you, and {polluted} air isn't).Still, sometimes our {assumptions} are {incorrect} , and scientific findings surprise researchers.That's because we have no access to first-hand information {unless} we actually {wander} through forests and {valleys} .A recent example is the phenomenon of {disappearing} lakes in parts of the {frozen} {treeless} Arctic region.
paragraphs.cn: 研究有时会用 <u> 数据 </u> 证明我们或多或少已经知道的事情（ <u> 例如 </u> ，锻炼对你有好处，而 <u> 污染 </u> 的空气则不然）。不过，有时我们的 <u> 假设 </u> 并 <u> 不正确 </u> ，科学研究发现会让研究人员感到惊讶。这是因为， <u> 除非 </u> 我们真的 <u> 漫步 </u> 于森林和 <u> 山谷 </u> 之中，否则我们无法获得第一手信息。最近的一个例子是，在北极地区一些终年 <u> 冰封 </u> 且 <u> 无树木生长的 </u> 区域湖泊逐渐 <u> 消失 </u> 的现象。

paragraphs.en: You might think these lakes would be expanding, not disappearing.As climate change warms the region—melting ( (融化) ) surface {snow} and {ice} as well as the permafrost ( (永冻层) )—there should be more surface water, forming larger lakes and even new ones.Recently, however, scientists have observed not just shrinking ( (缩小的) ) lakes but a {mass} disappearance of lakes.
paragraphs.cn: 你可能认为这些湖泊会扩大，而不是消失。随着气候变化使这片区域变暖——融化了 <u> 地表积雪 </u> 和冰层以及永冻层——地表水应该会变多，从而形成更大的湖泊，乃至新的湖泊。然而，最近科学家们不仅观察到湖泊缩小的情况，还发现湖泊在 <u> 大规模 </u> 消失。

paragraphs.en: Many scientists shared the commonsense expectation that as the {underground} permafrost melted, lakes would at first expand with meltwater ( (融水) ) flowing into them.Eventually, researchers made a prediction that {progressive} warming during the 21st and 22nd centuries would dry out the Arctic, and lakes would begin to shrink.But now it looks as if the {polar} waters are disappearing a century sooner than predicted.A case in point is that some large, {age-old} lakes shrank dramatically in a matter of months.Scientists have {labeled} this phenomenon“ {disastrous} lake loss”.
paragraphs.cn: 许多科学家都怀有一种常识性的预期，即随着 <u> 地下 </u> 永冻层的融化，湖泊首先会因融水的流入而扩大。最终，研究人员做出了一个预测，即在21世纪和22世纪， <u> 逐渐 </u> 变暖的气候会使北极地区干涸，而湖泊也将会开始缩小。然而，现在看来， <u> 极地 </u> 水域消失的时间似乎比原先预测的提前了一个世纪。一个典型的例子是，一些 <u> 古老的 </u> 大型湖泊在短短几个月内急剧缩小。科学家们 <u> 称 </u> 这一现象为“ <u> 灾难性的 </u> 湖泊流失”。

paragraphs.en: The permafrost is very solid, but in reality, there are spaces between the rocks, {minerals} , and organic matter that make it up.And because these spaces are filled with solid ice, like natural time {capsules} , {liquid} water cannot {readily} get inside, but it can when the permafrost {collapses} under the combined effects of warming and other factors, causing the water to {pour} away, leaving behind nothing but dry {basins} .Moreover, with the {liberation} of this ancient water, the trapped carbon is {released} , leading to further warming.
paragraphs.cn: 永冻层非常坚固，但实际上，构成永冻层的岩石、 <u> 矿物质 </u> 和有机物之间存在着空隙。这些空隙被像天然时间 <u> 胶囊 </u> 一样坚固的冰填满， <u> 液态 </u> 水无法 <u> 轻易地 </u> 渗入其中。但当永冻层在气候变暖和其他因素的共同作用下 <u> 崩塌 </u> 时，液态水就可以进入，使得水倾 <u> 泻 </u> 而下，留下的只有干涸的 <u> 盆地 </u> 。此外，随着这些古老水源被 <u> 释放 </u> 出来，被困的碳也随之 <u> 释放 </u> ，导致气候进一步变暖。

paragraphs.en: Why did scientists miss this? One {probable} reason is that most climate {models} assume that the melting of permafrost is driven only by warming air.However, new evidence suggests that {rainfall} —particularly increasing {autumn} rain—is now contributing significantly to permafrost loss.The rainfall carries heat into the ground.Yet {none} of the {existing} models includes such processes.
paragraphs.cn: 科学家们为什么忽视了这一点呢？一个 <u> 可能的 </u> 原因是，大多数气候 <u> 模型 </u> 都假定永冻层的融化仅由气温升高导致。然而，新的证据表明， <u> 降雨 </u> ——特别是不断增加的 <u> 秋季 </u> 降雨——在当前永冻层流失的过程中起到了重要的作用。降雨将热量带入了土地。然而， <u> 现有的 </u> 模型 <u> 都没有 </u> 考虑到这样的过程。

paragraphs.en: That is a good example of why—no matter how accurate our {statistics} are or will one day be—we need direct {observation} of the natural world.A {detective} must first go to the {crime} scene before piecing together evidence.Similarly, scientists should actively observe their subject, whether it's the smallest {cell} under a {microscope} or vast formations in a {cave} .
paragraphs.cn: 这是一个很好的例子，它说明，无论我们的 <u> 统计数据 </u> 有多准确，或者将来可能会有多准确，我们都需要对自然世界进行直接的 <u> 观察 </u> 。就像一名 <u> 侦探 </u> 必须先前往 <u> 犯罪 </u> 现场，然后才能将证据拼凑在一起一样。同样，科学家们也应该积极地观察研究对象，无论是 <u> 显微镜 </u> 下最微小的 <u> 细胞 </u> ，还是 <u> 洞穴 </u> 之中巨大的岩层构造。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
